$comment: The append-only half of the guard, for V's headless runs only.
This used to live in the vault's `.claude/settings.json`, next to the
privacy half. That put it on every Claude Code session opened in the
vault, including Parsa's own interactive ones, which was never the
intent: the rules exist to keep *V* off the in-place edit path, not to
stop a human at the keyboard from writing a note.
It cannot be split by setting source. `ClaudeCodeShell` runs with
`--setting-sources project,local`, and an interactive session loads
`user,project,local` — V's sources are a strict subset of Parsa's, so no
source exists that V reads and he does not. `--settings` is the way out:
it loads an *additional* file at highest precedence, and only V passes it.
Why the rules are needed at all: `shells.HOST_WRITE_TOOLS` grants Write,
Edit and NotebookEdit on any writing run, so V can touch the scripts and
configs at the vault root. Nothing else stops those same tools from
rewriting a note in place — no `[bot]` commit, no `v undo`. These four
patterns are that stop. `tests/test_shell.py` and `tests/test_mcp.py`
assert they stay in agreement with the granted tool list and with the
numbered folders actually on disk.
Scoped to the numbered vault folders rather than `**/*.md`, because the
broad pattern also caught developer docs — files that are code, not
notes, and have no append-only guarantee to protect.
Added 2026-11-08, with source labels (`core/provenance.py`):
Read on notes is denied so the model reads them through `vault_read`,
which fences V's unapproved text. A raw Read would hand it V's old
suggestions with nothing to tell them from Parsa's plans. Grep stays
open; it returns lines, and the system prompt says to `vault_read` a
note before relying on one.
The approval commands and the files approvals live in are denied too.
Approval is Parsa's act, and the real fence is that nothing the model is
granted calls an approval writer. These rules, and the V_MODEL_SHELL
variable the approval writers refuse under, are a second fence for the
one tool nothing binds completely: Bash.
